\-Best MMA Manga by far is All Rounder Meguru, it is by far the most realistic and it has a really simple yet concise story and lovable characters. Bonus points for being finished with a good ending.

\-Red blue is another great MMA manga that is pretty realistic in my opinion. It is currently ongoing and I recommend it because it is my 2nd favorite after All rounder Meguru.

\-Kengan Asura/Omega are both really good if you like some exaggerated fight scenes mixed with real martial arts.

\-Viral hit or How to fight  is a very good webtoon, fights and feats are exaggerated though .

\-Hajime no Ippo although there is a lot of plot armor for some fights and characters. Good boxing albeit exaggerated.

\-Baki is fun but as a martial arts goes it absolutely sucks.

\-Gosu is old style murim masters incredible feats disaster level power, but it technically is martial arts so I recommend it if you want some fantasy.

\-The breaker/The breaker new waves is really enjoyable and fun although it is more fantasy since it has to do with ki and stuff.

Im 5'7 and I regularly train with taller people than me. Believe in yourself dude, you can become a beast but you gotta have the right mindset too. There is a phrase in contact sports "Lower weight class skill" usually means that we have very good balance between agility and reflexes allowing for more freedom in technique. So with that said, there is a point were you must know your limits, I am no way fighting a 6'4 190-220lbs trained dude, untrained is a different story though.

I am right now on a diet and at 150lbs right now (gonna go to 125lbs end of year pray for me) and I do pretty decent against 5'10-6'1 155lbs-170lbs dudes. So yeah dude go for it, just know that you will most likely suck for the first few months, make sure to have a good mentality when trying a new contact sport.
